report.tagline: An app that sells fresh, cleaned and cut chicken, mutton and fish, delivered cold to your door, often in 30 minutes.
report.simpleSummary: Buying meat in India usually means a trip to a local butcher, where hygiene and freshness are a guess. Licious lets you order chicken, mutton, fish, eggs and ready-to-cook items on an app. It cuts and packs the meat in its own clean processing centres, keeps it cold the whole way, and delivers it to your home. You pay a bit more than at the butcher, but you know what you are getting.

keyNumbers.label: Revenue, FY26 (April 2025 to March 2026)
keyNumbers.value: ₹1,166 crore, up 47% from ₹795 crore in FY25
keyNumbers.note: Company claim reported by Inc42, 2026. Audited FY26 filings were not yet public at the time.

keyNumbers.label: Cash burn (EBITDA loss), FY26
keyNumbers.value: About ₹187 crore, up from about ₹168 crore in FY25
keyNumbers.note: Inc42, 2026. Loss grew because of new dark stores and offline shops.

keyNumbers.label: Net loss, FY25
keyNumbers.value: ₹218 crore, down 27% from ₹299 crore in FY24
keyNumbers.note: Regulatory filings reported by Inc42 and Entrackr, late 2025.

keyNumbers.label: Monthly active users
keyNumbers.value: Over 1.5 million; repeat customers make up about 94% of the business

keyNumbers.label: Funding
keyNumbers.value: Over $550 million raised; unicorn ($1 billion+ value) since 2021
keyNumbers.note: Investors include Temasek and 3one4 Capital. Reports in 2025 said Licious aims for an IPO at about $2 billion value; timing not confirmed.

keyNumbers.label: Offline sales
keyNumbers.value: ₹177 crore in FY26, up from ₹26 crore in FY25, from 60+ stores
keyNumbers.note: Inc42, 2026. Licious treats stores mainly as a trust-building channel.

overview.whatItDoes: Licious sells raw meat, seafood, eggs, cold cuts and marinated ready-to-cook items through its app, website, its own stores and quick commerce apps like Blinkit. It was started in Bengaluru in 2015 by Vivek Gupta and Abhay Hanjura. It owns the whole chain from buying from farms to cutting, packing and delivery, which is called farm-to-fork.
howItWorks: Licious buys chicken, goat and fish from farms and fishermen it has vetted, and checks quality at collection centres.
Meat is cut, cleaned and packed in its own processing centres, then kept between 0 and 4°C in the cold chain (refrigerated storage and transport at every step).
Packs go to dark stores, small warehouses near homes that only serve online orders.
You order on the app and pick a slot or the 30-minute Flash delivery, which about 55% of online users get.
A rider brings it in an insulated bag; you pay per pack, with a delivery fee on small orders unless you have the Meatopia membership.
overview.valueProposition: Meat you can trust: cleaned, cut the way you want, cold and fresh, at your door in about 30 minutes, without visiting a butcher.

painPoints.pain: Not trusting the hygiene at local butcher shops
painPoints.howSolved: Meat is cut in temperature-controlled centres and sealed in tamper-proof packs.

painPoints.pain: Meat going warm and spoiling on the way home
painPoints.howSolved: A cold chain keeps it at 0 to 4°C until delivery.

painPoints.pain: Cleaning and cutting fish or chicken takes time and is messy
painPoints.howSolved: Choose the exact cut: curry cut, boneless, fillet, cleaned prawns.

painPoints.pain: Weight and quality cheating at small shops
painPoints.howSolved: Fixed weight and fixed price printed on each pack.

painPoints.pain: Needing meat fast for a sudden plan or guests
painPoints.howSolved: Flash delivery in about 30 minutes in covered areas.

painPoints.pain: Not knowing how to marinate or cook well
painPoints.howSolved: Ready-to-cook marinades, kebabs and recipes in the app.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Each product shows cut type, weight, pieces per pack and serves.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Removes the main reason people trust a known butcher: getting the cut they want.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Delivers from the nearest dark store in about 30 minutes.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Competes with quick commerce apps that also sell meat now.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A paid plan that gives free delivery and extra discounts for a few months.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Locks in heavy users and raises repeat orders, which is where profit comes from.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Marinated chicken, kebabs, cold cuts, spreads and snacks.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Higher margin than raw chicken and helps beginners cook non-veg.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Report a bad pack in the app with a photo for a refund or replacement.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Trust is the whole product. One bad pack can lose a customer.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Licious packs sold in its 60+ stores and on quick commerce apps.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Finds new buyers who would not download a meat-only app.

steps.detail: Sees a Licious ad on Instagram or a friend's recommendation.
Checks that Licious delivers to their pin code.
Opens Chicken, compares curry cut vs boneless, reads weight and serves.
Picks Flash or a later slot.
Gets a cold sealed pack, checks smell and colour.
If it tastes fresh, they are likely to order again.
Adds the usual chicken and prawns in two taps.
Adds a marinated kebab pack suggested at checkout.
Watches the order arrive in about 30 minutes.

userJourneys.name: Quality complaint
userJourneys.persona: Seafood lover in a non-coastal city

steps.detail: Fish smells off when the pack is opened.
Goes to the order in the app and picks 'quality issue'.
Takes a picture of the product.
Receives a refund to the Licious wallet or a replacement.
A fast, fair fix keeps them; a slow one sends them to FreshToHome or Blinkit.

businessModel.summary: Licious makes money by selling meat it buys, processes and packs itself, at a markup over the farm price. It also earns delivery fees and membership fees, and sells through stores and other apps.

revenueStreams.stream: Product sales on its app and website
revenueStreams.detail: Over ₹1,000 crore in FY26; the main source of money.
Packs sold through apps like Blinkit, Zepto and Swiggy Instamart, which take a cut.
Small fees on low-value orders and a paid plan for free delivery.

businessModel.pricing: Per-pack prices on the app. For example, chicken curry cut 500g is often around ₹170 to ₹200, more than a local shop. A delivery fee applies below a minimum cart value unless you have Meatopia. Prices vary by city.
costDrivers: Raw meat and fish bought from farms (the biggest cost)
Cold chain: processing centres, refrigeration, insulated transport
Wastage: meat and fish spoil in days, so unsold stock is lost
Rent and staff for dark stores and offline shops
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate on a ₹600 order: about ₹360 to ₹400 is the cost of meat, about ₹60 to ₹80 goes to processing, packaging and cold storage, about ₹50 to ₹70 to delivery, plus wastage and marketing. That leaves little or nothing, which is why Licious still loses money (₹187 crore EBITDA loss in FY26 on ₹1,166 crore revenue, about 16 paise lost on each rupee). It earns more on repeat customers, bigger baskets and ready-to-cook items, which have better margins.

howTheyGetUsers: Performance ads on Instagram, YouTube and Google with first-order discounts
Being listed on Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart so people try the brand
Offline stores that let people see and trust the product
whatBringsUsersBack: Consistent quality: same taste and cut every time
Weekly cooking habit, especially weekend non-veg meals
Reorder from past orders in a few taps
growth.moat: Licious owns its full supply chain, from farm sourcing to cold processing centres to dark stores. Building that takes years and hundreds of crores, and it is hard to run without wastage. Its brand is also the best known name for packaged fresh meat in Indian metros.

competitors.name: Local butcher shops
competitors.positioning: Cheap, nearby and familiar; the default for most Indians.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Licious is cleaner, more consistent and delivered, but costs more.

competitors.name: FreshToHome
competitors.positioning: Online fish and meat brand, strong in seafood and South India.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Licious has a bigger brand in metros and a faster 30-minute delivery in many areas.

competitors.name: Zepto Relish, Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart
competitors.positioning: Quick commerce apps selling their own or partner meat in 10 minutes.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Licious has more cuts and fish choice; quick commerce wins on speed and one app for all shopping.

competitors.name: Meatigo (ITC) and Tendercuts
competitors.positioning: Packaged meat brands; ITC brings a big food company's backing.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Licious is bigger online and owns more of its delivery network.

northStar.why: Licious only wins if people trust the meat. An order that arrives cold, on time and fresh is the value delivered, and it predicts the next order.

App rating on Play Store and App Store

strengths: Strongest brand for trusted packaged meat in Indian metros
Owns the full cold supply chain, which is hard to copy
Very high repeat business (about 94% of sales from repeat buyers)
Revenue growing fast again (47% in FY26) after a flat period
Multiple channels: app, own stores and quick commerce apps

Prices higher than local butchers, which limits reach outside metros
Perishable stock means high wastage risk
Only one category, so customers open the app less often than a grocery app

Big food companies like ITC entering packaged meat
Food safety incidents can damage trust quickly

Prices feel high compared with the local shop
Refunds sometimes go only to the Licious wallet, not the bank

improvementIdeas.idea: Show 'packed at' date and time on every product page and pack
improvementIdeas.problem: Users worry about freshness, especially for fish.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trust, fewer complaints, higher conversion on seafood.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Seafood conversion rate and quality complaint rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Instant refund to original payment method for photo-verified quality issues
improvementIdeas.problem: Wallet-only refunds and slow support make users angry and push them to rivals.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better retention after a bad order.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Repeat rate of users who raised a complaint

improvementIdeas.idea: Smaller single-serve packs (250g) for one-person homes
improvementIdeas.problem: Bachelors find packs too big and the cart too costly.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More orders from young single users.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: New customers aged 18 to 25 and their 30-day repeat rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Weekly subscription for the usual weekend order
improvementIdeas.problem: Weekend stock-outs and the effort of reordering.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Predictable demand, lower wastage, higher orders per user.

improvementIdeas.idea: Price match on top 5 chicken cuts against a city benchmark
improvementIdeas.problem: Price is the top reason people stay with local butchers.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Win price-sensitive families into the habit, then upsell ready-to-cook.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: New customer growth and gross margin per order

pmLessons: In food, trust is the product. Licious sells the same chicken as a butcher; what people pay extra for is confidence that it is clean and fresh.
Owning the supply chain is expensive but gives control over quality. It is a moat and a cost burden at the same time.
A single-category app has to fight harder for frequency. Licious grows by selling through other apps and stores, not only its own app.
Watch wastage as closely as sales. With perishable goods, each extra store adds stock that can spoil.

interviewQuestions.question: Quick commerce apps now deliver meat in 10 minutes. How should Licious respond?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick what Licious does better (cuts, seafood, freshness proof). Decide whether to compete on speed or on quality. Suggest 2 to 3 moves and a metric like repeat rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Licious sees a rise in quality complaints in one city. How do you find the cause?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break by product, store, time of day and step in the chain. Check temperature logs and supplier batches. Fix the root, then track complaint rate per 1,000 orders.

interviewQuestions.question: What should be Licious's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Choose something showing value to users, like fresh on-time orders with no complaint. Break it into repeat users, quality, delivery and basket size.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Licious open more offline stores or more dark stores?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cost, new customers won, trust and margin. Offline builds trust; dark stores drive repeat online orders. Suggest a test in one city.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to get a first-time user to their second order.
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why people do not return (price, doubt, forgot). Propose a reminder plus a second-order offer tied to what they bought. Measure 30-day repeat rate.

glossary.meaning: When one company controls every step from buying from farms to delivering food to the eater.
Keeping food refrigerated at every step from processing to your door so it does not spoil.
Small warehouses near homes that only pack online orders and are closed to walk-in shoppers.
Apps like Blinkit and Zepto that deliver everyday items in 10 to 30 minutes.
Earnings before interest, tax and accounting charges for wear of assets; a rough measure of whether day-to-day operations make or lose money.
A private startup valued at $1 billion or more.
Initial public offering: when a company first sells shares on the stock market.
The one number a team watches to know if users are getting real value.
The average amount a customer spends in one order.
The share of customers who stop using a product in a period.
What is left from one order after paying the direct costs of that order, like product, packing and delivery.
